topic: Your phone weakens your thinking even when you are not using it
subject: technology

facts.claim: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity, even when people successfully avoid the temptation to check them.
facts.quote: Results from two experiments indicate that even when people are successful at maintaining sustained attention—as when avoiding the temptation to check their phones—the mere presence of these devices reduces available cognitive capacity.

facts.claim: A meta-analysis found that the mere presence of a smartphone negatively impacts working memory capacity, but has no significant effect on other cognitive functions.
facts.quote: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while results for the remaining cognitive functions produced null summary effects.

facts.claim: Participants with higher positive urgency showed increased cognitive interference in a silent-mode smartphone condition compared to a turned-off smartphone condition.
facts.quote: The results showed that participants with higher positive urgency presented increased cognitive interference (reflected by poorer task performance) in the "silent-mode smartphone" condition compared with participants in the "turned-off smartphone" condition.

facts.claim: The cognitive costs of a smartphone's presence are highest for people who have a high level of smartphone dependence.
facts.quote: Moreover, these cognitive costs are highest for those highest in smartphone dependence.

facts.claim: An experiment on participants aged 20-34 showed that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance.
facts.quote: The results of the conducted experiment imply that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance, which supports the hypothesis of the smartphone presence using limited cognitive resources.

rejected.claim: A meta-analysis of 33 studies found that the mere presence of a smartphone had no significant effect on cognitive outcomes (d = −0. 02, SE = 0. 02, 95% CI [−0. 06, 0. 01], p = . 246).
rejected.quote: It was found that the mere presence of smartphone had no significant effect on cognitive outcomes (d = −0. 02, SE = 0. 02, 95% CI [−0. 06, 0. 01], p = . 246).

research.angle: While some experiments suggest a 'brain drain' effect on cognitive capacity and working memory, a large meta-analysis found no significant effect on cognitive outcomes.
research.verdict: The evidence is mixed, with some studies showing reduced cognitive capacity and others finding no significant impact on performance.
research.caveat: The research is characterized by substantial methodological heterogeneity and generally poor statistical power.
